title: Grafana 13.3 Adds Shared Dashboard Variables and Notebooks
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/grafana-13-3-shared-variables/en/headerimage/header-1795209346746.jpeg"/><p>Grafana 13.3 introduces shared variables across dashboards and adds Notebooks to record investigations. Both features are in public preview and require feature toggles for self-managed installations.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Scaling Tech by Aligning Humans
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/scalling-tech-humans/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795181753113.jpg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco 2026, Scott Behrens, Principal Security Engineer at Netflix, presented how staff-plus engineers can define and align a company-wide technical strategy.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

title: How Google Traced GKE API Timeouts to a Linux Kernel TCP Bug
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/gke-kernel-network-bug/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794082671635.jpg"/><p>Google recently detailed how three interacting bugs across Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), Private Service Connect, and the Linux kernel caused intermittent Kubernetes API connectivity failures, blocking around 800 developers from deploying to production.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Meta TLX, a Native GPU Compiler Extension Supporting Advanced Hardware Capabilities
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/meta-triton-tlx-gpu-compiler/en/headerimage/meta-java-kotlin-port-1795195032767.jpeg"/><p>Meta developed Triton Low-Level Extensions (TLX), designed to bridge the gap between high-level GPU programming abstractions and the low-level execution control required to fully exploit modern GPU architectures.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Uber Cuts Translation Cache Memory by up to 90% While Keeping P99 Latency Below 1 MS
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Uber redesigned its Go-based translation cache to reduce its initial memory footprint by more than 90% while maintaining a cache hit rate above 99.9% and p99 disk-backed cache miss latency below 100 microseconds. The hybrid architecture combines in-memory keys and frequently accessed values with disk-backed storage, reducing garbage-collection overhead and memory consumption.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Google Donates Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF to Secure AI Agents at Scale
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-substrate-gvisor-cncf/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794408775099.jpg"/><p>Google has announced it is donating Agent Substrate and gVisor to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), placing two important components of its AI agent infrastructure under vendor-neutral open-source governance.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: Modernising Retail at Scale: Architecting a Cloud‑to‑Edge Platform for a Global Enterprise
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/tesco-enterprise-tech-transformation/en/mediumimage/JayeshBhayani-medium-1792654742095.jpg"/><p>Jayesh Bhayani discusses Tesco’s decade-long enterprise transformation from fragmented legacy systems to a unified cloud-edge platform. He explains how aligning system, talent, and process modernizations allowed Tesco to scale mission-critical retail operations to millions of customers, while sharing practical lessons on build vs. buy, cloud cost management, and preparing for agentic commerce.</p> <i>By Jayesh Bhayani</i>

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: The Future of Apache Iceberg
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/iceberg-v4-metadata/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795116071082.jpg"/><p>Apache Iceberg V4 proposes a redesign of table metadata to improve scalability and support more frequent writes, alongside new capabilities for data management and schema evolution. Daniel Weeks, co-creator of Apache Iceberg and member of technical staff at Databricks, presented a session at QCon San Francisco on the fourth version of the Apache Iceberg open table format specification.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Article: Building Reliability Into the Cloud: Observability as the Control Plane for Multi-Region Failover
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/observability-control-plane-failover/en/headerimage/header-1795002929606.jpg"/><p>Cloud SLAs promise uptime statistically, not absolutely. This article shows how to treat observability as a control plane that detects regional degradation, triggers automated failover, and confirms recovery rather than paging a human. Covers active-active architecture, DNS TTL pitfalls, composite Prometheus alerting, Route 53 weighted routing, and confirmation loops backed by a real S3 outage.</p> <i>By Saurabh Ahuja</i>

title: AWS Releases a Free Local Emulator of AWS Built Entirely by Agents
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-emulator-local-testing/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795086946449.jpg"/><p>AWS has released AWS Emulator, a free, CC0-licensed local stand-in for more than 200 of its services, generated from its public API models and aimed at the test loops of coding agents. AWS says agents wrote and maintain all of the code and publishes per-release fidelity scores. The docs say it does not evaluate IAM, and practitioners are split on trusting an emulator nobody reviewed.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Presentation: AI-Assisted Software Delivery: From Code to Production
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-assisted-software-delivery/en/mediumimage/infoq-live-medium-1795097572325.jpg"/><p>The panelists explore how engineering teams adapt delivery architectures, pipelines, security, and governance for AI-assisted development. They share practical strategies for verifying AI-generated code, solving testing and deployment bottlenecks, maintaining human oversight, and measuring AI’s true impact on software velocity, quality, reliability, and operational cost.</p> <i>By Garima Bajpaj, Martin Reynolds, Patrick Debois, Gunnar Grosch, Renato Losio</i>

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Use AI to Multiply Your Team as a Staff Engineer
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/ai-staff-engineer/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795089716434.jpg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco 2026, Jordan Cutler, Senior Staff Engineer and Web Platform Tech Lead at Pinterest, presented how the role of a staff engineer changes when every engineer has access to the same AI tools.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

title: .NET 11 : ASP.NET Core: Union Type Support, OpenAPI 3.2 by Default and Blazor AI Components
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Microsoft has released ASP.NET Core in .NET 11. The update adds C# union type support in JSON bodies, asynchronous validation for Minimal APIs, OpenAPI 3.2 by default, and SignalR authentication refresh. Blazor gains a CacheView component, client-side validation for static SSR forms, opt-in circuit pause for inactive tabs, and experimental AI components. Zstandard compression is on by default.</p> <i>By Almir Vuk</i>

title: Producing Healthy Code with Artificial Intelligence Costs Fewer Tokens
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/healthy-code-AI-tokens/en/headerimage/header-1794837764807.jpg"/><p>Agentic AI can speed up velocity, but the gains vanish within months as code complexity grows.  Healthy code makes AI perform better and costs fewer tokens. Safeguarding means keeping code health high through agentic refactoring, with an MCP supplying code health data, so AI can maintain the code it generates.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

title: Presentation: RIIIR: Rewrite It In *Idiomatic* Rust (with AI)
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/rust-ai-symposium-agent-client-protocol/en/mediumimage/NikoMatsakis-medium-1793279155828.jpeg"/><p>Nicholas Matsakis shares why AI makes Rust the ideal choice for modern production systems, skipping steep adoption hurdles via compiler guardrails. He discusses Symposium - an open-source, agent-oriented toolchain from the Rust Foundation - and demonstrates how the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) standardizes agent-to-tool extensibility across diverse enterprise developer workflows.</p> <i>By Niko Matsakis</i>
